items.title: Diabetes leaders named among UK’s most influential ethnic minority figures in healthcare
items.summary: Two leading figures whose work has helped shape diabetes research, prevention and care have been recognised in a prestigious list of the UK’s most influential Black, Asian and minority ethnic people in health.

items.title: Experts warn of missed opportunities to detect kidney disease in people with diabetes
items.summary: Thousands of people living with diabetes could be missing out on early detection of chronic kidney disease because of low uptake of a simple urine test, kidney health experts have warned.

items.title: Antipsychotic diabetes risk ‘peaks in first 90 days’
items.summary: The first 90 days after being prescribed antipsychotics is the most crucial period for monitoring patients’ risk of developing diabetes, new research has suggested.

items.title: Free webinar series to support pharmacists in diabetes and obesity care
items.summary: The Diabetes & Obesity Pharmacy Alliance is launching a series of free webinars to help pharmacists navigate the evolving landscape of diabetes and obesity care, with sessions exploring injectable therapies, medicines optimisation and the complexities of patient care.

items.title: Ascensia announces strategic partnership with Sava for innovative microsensor technology
items.summary: A new wearable microsensor designed to make glucose monitoring less invasive could be available in Europe within the next two years, following a partnership between Ascensia Diabetes Care and Sava Technologies.

items.title: Study shows low energy diet combined with structured exercise reverses early onset type 2 diabetes in half of participants
items.summary: New research published in The Lancet Regional Health Americas shows that around half of people diagnosed with early-onset type 2 diabetes before the age of 45 can achieve remission through a low-energy diet combined with a structured exercise programme.

items.title: Once-weekly insulin jab for type 2 diabetes authorised by MHRA
items.summary: A new once-weekly insulin treatment for adults with type 2 diabetes has been authorised by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA). Onswik (insulin efsitora alfa) is a long-acting basal insulin that could cut the injections needed by patients currently on daily treatment from 365 a year to 52.

items.title: The Kar Report: Is it time to stop trying to do everything in diabetes care?
items.summary: In the first of a new opinion series, Dr Partha Kar questions whether NHS diabetes care has reached a tipping point – and whether prioritising just three key areas could be the bold decision needed to reverse declining standards. Let’s be honest. We are in troubling times.

items.title: Final call to register for CVRM Professional Care as conference chair announces collaboration is key to helping sustain the NHS
items.summary: The organisers of an inaugural conference which will bring together experts in diabetes, cardiovascular, renal and metabolic care have issued a final call to secure one of the last remaining tickets.

items.title: Rethinking nursing practice for early-onset type 2 diabetes
items.summary: British Journal of Nursing, Volume 35, Issue 18, Page 898-900, October 2026.

items.title: University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust has been named the winner of the Insulin Safety Week Excellence Award
items.summary: University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust has been presented with the Insulin Safety Week Excellence Award in recognition of its outstanding contribution to this year’s campaign.

items.title: Smart insulin pen alerts linked to improved glucose outcomes in type 1 diabetes
items.summary: People with type 1 diabetes using multiple daily injections who respond more consistently to smart insulin pen alerts could achieve improved glucose outcomes, according to new six-month randomised trial data.

items.title: New type 1 diabetes guidance targets misdiagnosis in adults
items.summary: New guidance on the management of type 1 diabetes in adults has put greater emphasis on accurate diagnosis amid concerns that the condition is frequently mistaken for type 2 diabetes in people diagnosed later in life.

items.title: CareSens Air achieves maximum 5/5 rating in DSN Forum UK CGM Comparison Chart
items.summary: Spirit Health and manufacturing partner i-SENS are celebrating CareSens Air achieving the maximum 5/5 study design score in the latest DSN Forum UK CGM Comparison Chart.

items.title: Native collagen matrix plus PHMB antimicrobial in hard-to-heal diabetic foot ulcers: results from the PREPARE randomised controlled trial
items.summary:

items.title: Guideline on diabetes distress calls for routine emotional checks
items.summary: Healthcare professionals should routinely discuss the emotional impact of diabetes with patients, according to a clinical practice guideline developed by the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD).

items.title: EASD 2026: Primary care is ‘fundamental’ to tackling global burden of diabetes, researchers stress
items.summary: Primary care is “uniquely positioned” to drive improvements in diabetes care and tackle this “major global public health crisis”, East Midlands researchers have argued.

items.summary: MID CHESHIRE HOSPITALS NHS FOUNDATION TRUST. Supply of Dexcom G6/G7…

items.title: Faster alignment of technology appraisals with clinical guidelines trialled in type 2 diabetes update
items.summary: Four technology appraisals for type 2 diabetes have been updated, and guidance on 4 further medicines is being withdrawn, as part of NICE’s first test of a new way of keeping all its guidance aligned. NICE recently updated its guideline on type 2 diabetes in adults.

items.title: EASD 2026: Study finds reassuring signs for diabetic and weight loss drug use around pregnancy, but questions remain
items.summary: A study by an international group of researchers finds popular diabetes and weight-loss drugs are not linked to pregnancy complications in most women with diabetes.

items.title: GLP-1s and SGLT-2s may help slow kidney damage in diabetes, study shows
items.summary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor drugs slow decline in kidney function in people with type 2 diabetes, but the benefits are only seen if they also have albuminuria, a large US ‘real-world’ study has reported.

items.title: EASD 2026: Type 2 diabetes outcomes classified to strengthen disease modification efforts
items.summary: A new framework which categorises the outcomes of type 2 diabetes could be instrumental in the drive to alter the progression of the disease and prevent complications.

items.title: Debbie Hicks steps down as Chair of Trend Diabetes
items.summary: Debbie Hicks is stepping down as Chair of Trend Diabetes after almost two decades with the organisation, as she prepares to embark on a new chapter travelling the world and ticking off her bucket list.

items.title: Abbott, Medtronic, Dexcom and 9 others win NHS Scotland's £140m insulin pump and CGM framework
items.summary: NHS National Services Scotland has awarded a new £140 million framework for insulin infusion pumps, continuous glucose monitoring systems and associated consumables, covering all NHS Scotland health boards and NHS Northern Ireland trusts.

items.title: New diabetes safety training aims to reduce avoidable inpatient harm
items.summary: The Cambridge Diabetes Education Programme (CDEP) has launched a new competency-based training topic to give hospital trusts a practical, scalable and auditable way to equip staff with essential diabetes safety knowledge.

items.title: EASD 2026: CGM use linked to lower mortality and hospitalisation risk in Type 2 diabetes
items.summary: New real-world data to be presented at EASD 2026 suggest continuous glucose monitoring could have benefits extending beyond glycaemic management for people with Type 2 diabetes using basal insulin, with CGM use associated with lower mortality, cardiovascular complications and acute diabetes-related hospitalisations.

items.title: CKD Connect launches with webinar to support healthcare professionals in earlier recognition and management
items.summary: Healthcare professionals are being offered new educational support to help recognise chronic kidney disease (CKD) earlier and strengthen its ongoing management as part of a new National Kidney Federation (NKF) campaign.

items.title: Persistent ketoacidosis risk found with SGLT2 diabetes drugs
items.summary: Patients taking widely used SGLT2 inhibitor drugs for type 2 diabetes can remain at risk of ketoacidosis throughout treatment, a large Scandinavian study suggests. Ketoacidosis is a potentially life-threatening complication caused by a build-up of ketones in the blood.

items.title: Cancer incidence remains higher in people with type 2 diabetes, with the gap widening in recent years, study reveals
items.summary: A nationwide study being presented at the Annual Meeting of The European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) in Milan, Italy (Sept 28 – Oct 2) has found that people with type 2 diabetes have a higher risk of developing cancer, with cancer incidence rising more than those without diabetes over the past…

items.title: CLEAR study seeks UK participants to investigate restoring hypo awareness
items.summary: A major international trial is recruiting people with type 1 diabetes to investigate whether diabetes technology, psychoeducation or a combination of the two is most effective at restoring impaired awareness of hypoglycaemia.

items.title: Kidney Research UK and Royal College of Nursing come together to strengthen kidney care
items.summary: Kidney Research UK and the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) have joined forces to develop a new resource designed to help nurses identify and manage chronic kidney disease (CKD), including among people living with diabetes.

items.title: Newer diabetes drugs linked with reduced kidney risk in some patients
items.summary: Newer treatments for type 2 diabetes have been shown to slow down the progression of chronic kidney disease in patients with high protein levels in their urine, according to a study out this week.
